hypothesis_updates.claim: For 2,6-dimethoxybenzaldehyde at PE/EA 1/1 and 150 µL sample volume, V2 with 500 µL DCM exceeds V2 with 300 µL DCM by at least 10 mL.
hypothesis_updates.relevance_to_model_learning: One label completes the comparison across two ratios and two preparation volumes, testing whether the model needs a ratio-dependent loading-solvent-volume response.
hypothesis_updates.revision_reason: At 2/1 the larger DCM preparation gave later V2 at both 100 and 150 µL sample volumes. At 5/1 and 50 µL sample volume the preparations differed by only 2.01 mL, with the opposite ordering.
hypothesis_updates.unresolved_question: With V2 measured at 39.38 mL for the 500 µL preparation at 1/1, does the matched 300 µL preparation end at or below 29.38 mL?

feedback_interpretation: At 5/1, 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol gave V2 values of 71.53, 19.14 and 72.41 mL at 50, 100 and 150 µL. The rebound motivates measuring the missing third load for the bromo analogue. For 2,6-dimethoxybenzaldehyde, the 500 µL DCM preparation gave later V2 at 2/1 at both matched loads, although the V1 difference changed sign. Cinnamic acid with 1500 µL DCM gave its latest measured V2 at 1/1, between earlier values at 0/1 and 2/1. These results favor testing the two endpoints separately and measuring intermediate ratios.
